recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future build shows this validation is missing for an extension pack or IG, follow up in Kindling/publisher or the affected external repository rather than changing HL7/fhir source for this historical core issue.
issue_request: FHIR-12276 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request from DSTU2 asking that the build tool reject extension definitions whose value type is code when the binding strength is not required, with QICore-AdverseEvent.severity as the example.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git commit 48770dbe1f6b54bb320aca9a3bf5644ddfd1b4e0, whose subject names #12276 and whose git-svn-id records build@11444. That commit added ExtensionDefinitionValidator.checkCodesHaveRequiredBinding and invoked extension validation after spreadsheet snapshot generation.
additional_context: The old tools/java build sources were removed from HL7/fhir by commit 9f549566d1346cad7db6d2afca6080d7cebdfbbe when the repository switched to Gradle and the external Kindling dependency. Current build configuration runs org.hl7.fhir.tools.publisher.Publisher from org.hl7.fhir:kindling version 1.25.5-SNAPSHOT, and that dependency's source jar still contains and invokes the code-valued extension binding check.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active core extension spreadsheet/XML sources were checked and had no code-valued extension definitions with non-required bindings; the authoritative build-tool behavior now lives in the Kindling dependency rather than editable HL7/fhir source.
